JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental case: Q1 2026 EPS of $5.94 grew +17.2% YoY, revenue hit $49.84B (+10% YoY), operating margin expanded to ~41.1%, and ROE improved to 16.2%. The franchise is elite — #1 global investment banking fees for 17 consecutive years, $4.8T AUM (+16% YoY), and diversified revenue across consumer, CIB, and AWM. However, the valuation picture is more nuanced than the quant report suggests. The advisory correction [C1/C2] flags a critical arithmetic inconsistency: PE of 14x on $5.94 EPS implies ~$83, not $303, meaning the PE denominator likely uses a different EPS basis (possibly TTM with a Q4 gap). This undermines the quant report's reversion math claiming +28% upside from median PE reversion. The stock at $303 is not clearly cheap on a forward basis if the PE is computed on incomplete TTM data. P/B at 2.26x is near the floor of its 12-month range (2.2–2.8), which provides some valuation support, but the qual report notes P/B of 2.3x vs 5-year average of 1.8x — meaning the stock is still rich versus longer-term history. The SpaceX IPO underwriting role (05/20/2026) is a credible near-term fee catalyst, and the NII guidance revision to ~$103B (05/14/2026) is modest and already absorbed. Balance-sheet growth of +12.4% YoY with equity-to-assets thinning to 7.4% and negative OCF of -$211.76B are real risk flags. On balance, excellent franchise quality and earnings momentum support a modestly positive score, but valuation is not as cheap as the quant report claims once the PE arithmetic is corrected, and the quality is consensus (15 Buy / 15 Hold). Score of +0.35 reflects strong fundamentals and trajectory (pillar 1) partially offset by valuation that is fair-to-slightly-cheap on P/B but ambiguous on PE (pillar 2), with a modest bump from the SpaceX catalyst (pillar 3).
